intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that recurrent hydatidiform mole-6 (HYDM6) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the KASH5 gene.

checks.claim: Recurrent hydatidiform mole-6 (HYDM6) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the KASH5 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: identified 2 variants, NM_144688:c.1555C>T, p.(Arg519*), and c.1604T>A, p.(Leu535Gln), in a heterozygous state
checks.explanation: The paper reports only one KASH5 patient, who carries 2 heterozygous variants that are most likely in trans. It reports no homozygous KASH5 case, so the homozygous part must come from another source.

paragraphs.text: Recurrent hydatidiform moles (RHMs) are defined by the occurrence of at least 2 hydatidiform moles (HMs) in the same patient, and some are familial (Rezaei et al., 2024). HMs are abnormal human pregnancies with impaired embryonic development and excessive trophoblastic proliferation. Saharan et al. (2026) noted the potential for progression to metastatic gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) in patients with KASH5 variants.

checks.claim: Recurrent hydatidiform moles (RHMs) are defined by the occurrence of at least 2 hydatidiform moles in the same patient.
checks.evidence_quote: Recurrent HMs (RHMs) are defined by the occurrence of at least 2 HMs in the same patient
checks.explanation: The paper states this definition directly.

checks.claim: Some recurrent hydatidiform moles are familial.
checks.evidence_quote: and some of them are familial, occurring in at least 2 family members.
checks.explanation: The paper states that some recurrent moles are familial.

checks.claim: Hydatidiform moles are abnormal human pregnancies with impaired embryonic development and excessive trophoblastic proliferation.
checks.evidence_quote: Hydatidiform moles (HMs) are abnormal human pregnancies with impaired embryonic development and excessive trophoblastic proliferation.
checks.explanation: The paper states this description directly.

checks.claim: Patients with KASH5 variants have the potential to progress to metastatic gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN).
checks.evidence_quote: Our findings further support the association of variants in these genes with RHM while highlighting the potential for severe, life-threatening progression to metastatic GTN.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this potential for patients with these variants.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of HYDM6 in the patients reported by Rezaei et al. (2024) and Saharan et al. (2026) is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance. Rezaei et al. (2024) found compound heterozygous variants, and Saharan et al. (2026) found a homozygous variant.

checks.evidence_quote: recessive P/LP variants in the 9 genes (n = 15 patients)
checks.explanation: The paper treats the KASH5 variants as biallelic and recessive, which is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.evidence_quote: only one of them, p.R519*, was inherited from her mother, and therefore, the 2 variants are most likely on 2 different parental chromosomes.
checks.explanation: The paper only says the variants are 'most likely' on different parental chromosomes, because only maternal segregation was shown. It does not state outright that they are compound heterozygous.

paragraphs.text: Rezaei et al. (2024) performed whole-exome sequencing on 75 unrelated patients with at least 2 HMs who were negative for recessive mutations in NLRP7 and KHDC3L. In a Jordanian woman (patient 439) with RHM, they identified 2 heterozygous variants in the KASH5 gene: c.1555C-T, resulting in an arg519-to-ter (R519X) substitution, and c.1604T-A, resulting in a leu535-to-gln (L535Q) substitution. Sanger sequencing confirmed both variants in the proband. Only R519X was inherited from her mother, so the authors concluded that the 2 variants were most likely on different parental chromosomes. In the same study, biallelic variants in FOXL2, MAJIN, SYCP2, HFM1, and MEIOB were found in other patients.

paragraphs.text: Saharan et al. (2026) performed whole-exome sequencing in 2 women with RHM and validated selected candidate variants by Sanger sequencing. In 1 patient, who had recurrent GTNs, they identified a very rare homozygous variant in KASH5, arg196-to-his (R196H). In the other patient they identified a heterozygous variant in FOXL2, gly187-to-asp (G187D), which had been reported in patients with premature ovarian insufficiency.

paragraphs.text: Rezaei et al. (2024) noted that MAJIN and KASH5 mediate the attachment of telomeres to the nuclear envelope. This attachment is critical for homologous chromosome search and synapsis. The authors proposed that defects in meiotic synapsis and recombination play a major role in the formation of androgenetic complete HMs.

paragraphs.text: In a Jordanian woman with 3 HMs and 2 miscarriages, Rezaei et al. (2024) identified compound heterozygous mutations in the KASH5 gene: a c.1555C-T transition, resulting in an arg519-to-ter (R519X) substitution, and a c.1604T-A transversion, resulting in a leu535-to-gln (L535Q) substitution. They found the mutations by exome sequencing and confirmed them by Sanger sequencing. The R519X variant was inherited from the patient's mother. It had a CADD score of 36.

checks.claim: One KASH5 mutation in the Jordanian woman was a c.1555C-T transition resulting in an R519X substitution.
checks.explanation: The variant matches. A C>T change is a transition by definition.

checks.claim: The other KASH5 mutation in the Jordanian woman was a c.1604T-A transversion resulting in an L535Q substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: c.1604T>A, p.(Leu535Gln)
checks.explanation: The variant matches. A T>A change is a transversion by definition.

agent.process_note: I read the full text of Rezaei et al. (2024) and the abstract of Saharan et al. (2026), which is the only part available. No causal gene was supplied. I chose KASH5 because it is the only gene with biallelic variants in patients in both papers: compound heterozygous in Rezaei and homozygous in Saharan. FOXL2 was not treated as causal. Rezaei classified its FOXL2 missense variant as a VUS, and Saharan's FOXL2 variant was heterozygous. No reference data were provided, so the intro gives no gene MIM number or chromosome location. The KASH5 patient's molar tissue was not reported as genotyped, so I did not attribute an androgenetic genotype to KASH5 moles. The Saharan abstract gives no nucleotide change for R196H and no GTN rates from its literature review.
